critique.verdict: misreads edge — teaches IK technique, not embodiment tension
critique.paragraph: This plate teaches articulated joint hierarchies and inverse kinematics — a technical implementation pattern — rather than the phenomenological mismatch between continuous bodies and discrete algorithms. The purple wave pattern hints at continuous motion, but there is no visible discrete apparatus to create tension against it. The spatial grammar reads as 'here is how FK/IK works' rather than 'the algorithm cannot hold the body.' The blurb confirms the misread: it describes constraint propagation and endpoint solving, not the lived experience of being quantised by a system not built for you. Edge E demands a dance floor that punishes smoothness or rewards grid-snapping; this map offers a kinematic demo.
strengths: Clean, minimal composition with centered teaching artifact
Purple wave pattern suggests continuous motion/flow vocabulary
Kinematic rig is legible as a joint chain structure
weaknesses: No discrete grid visible to contrast with continuous body motion
Blurb describes technical IK implementation, not body-algorithm phenomenology
No spatial grammar for quantisation apparatus or frame-stepping
Missing the 'dance for/beside algorithm' choice point specified in edge sketch
Scale too small to choreograph embodied tension across space
No Vitruvian/Marey/chronophotographic visual reference to signal discrete-continuous bracket
next_gen_hints: Replace IK artifact with grid-snapping dance floor that visually highlights when player motion quantises to discrete cells
Add visual trail system showing continuous VR controller path versus discrete algorithm interpretation (Marey-style motion frames)
Create two spatial paths: one rewarding grid-aligned movement, one punishing it — force player to choose dance grammar
Expand floor pattern to show chronophotographic frames of player body discretised across time-space
Add Vitruvian circle/square overlay that constrains body into geometric grid when activated
Introduce CA or automaton that advances only when player's gait matches its discrete rhythm
Show body-trace artifacts: continuous gesture frozen into discrete pose keyframes along path
critique.edge_reads_as: J (joining/composition technique) or K (kinematic implementation) — not E
